# Iran at War Test Reference Guide, Paste-Ready

**Generated by `scripts/build-canvas-events.js`. Do not hand-edit.**
The blank PDF is `docs/assessments/iran-reference-sheet.pdf`, built by `scripts/build-iran-reference-sheet.py`.

Students fill in a one-page, limited fillable PDF, submit it here, and use
**that submitted file** on the unit test. The test is locked until this
assignment is submitted. Canvas does the locking, through module
requirements, so nobody has to check by hand before the test opens.

## The assignment

**Assignment name, Canvas and PowerSchool, character for character:** `IR - Test Reference Guide`  
**Points:** 10  

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Submission type | Online, then **File Uploads** |
| Restrict upload file types | On, `pdf` |
| Attempts | Unlimited |
| Available until | The moment the test opens |
| Display grade as | Points |
| Peer review | Off |
| Anonymous grading | Off |

**File Uploads is right here, and only here.** Every other BeCurrent
assignment is Text Entry so the parser can read it. This one is the PDF
itself: the locked font size and the character limits are the point, and a
Text Entry box has neither.

**Available until the test opens**, so the file a student uses on the test
cannot change during it. Unlimited attempts before then: the last file
submitted is the one that counts.

### Put the blank PDF in the body

1. Paste the block below, or all of `docs/canvas/iran-reference-guide-body.html`, through the RCE **`</>`** HTML editor.
2. Switch back to the visual editor and select the line
   `[INSERT BLANK PDF FROM THE DOCUMENTS PANEL]`.
3. In the RCE toolbar choose **Documents**, then **Upload Document**, and upload `docs/assessments/iran-reference-sheet.pdf`.
   It replaces the placeholder with a link to the file, stored in this course.

```html
<h2>Iran at War: Test Reference Guide</h2>
<p><strong>What this is:</strong> a one-page guide you fill in with your own notes. You may use it on the Iran at War unit test.</p>
<p><strong>Due:</strong> Friday, October 2, before the test opens.</p>
<div style="border-left: 5px solid #CE1400; background-color: #f4f2ed; padding: 10px 14px; margin: 12px 0;">
<p><strong>Two rules to know before you start</strong></p>
<ol>
    <li><strong>The test stays locked until you turn this in.</strong> Once you submit your guide here, the test opens for you.</li>
    <li><strong>You may only use the guide you turn in here.</strong> Not a different copy, and not other notes.</li>
</ol>
</div>

<h3>Step 1: Download the blank guide</h3>
<p>[INSERT BLANK PDF FROM THE DOCUMENTS PANEL]</p>
<ol>
    <li>Click the link above.</li>
    <li>Click <strong>Download</strong>. The file saves to the <strong>Downloads</strong> folder on your Chromebook.</li>
</ol>

<h3>Step 2: Open it in Google Chrome</h3>
<ol>
    <li>Open the <strong>Files</strong> app and click <strong>Downloads</strong>.</li>
    <li>Right-click the guide (tap with two fingers), then choose <strong>Open with</strong> and <strong>Google Chrome</strong>.</li>
</ol>
<p>Use Chrome. The boxes do not work correctly in Kami or in the Canvas preview.</p>

<h3>Step 3: Fill in the boxes</h3>
<ul>
    <li>Click inside a box and type. Press <strong>Tab</strong> to jump to the next box.</li>
    <li>Every box has a size limit. <strong>When a box stops taking text, it is full.</strong> Pick what matters most.</li>
    <li>The font and text size are locked. You cannot change them, and you cannot paste more than a box can show.</li>
    <li>Short notes fit best: keywords, arrows (like 1953 &rarr; distrust), and abbreviations.</li>
    <li>Not sure what to include? Use the <a class="inline_disabled" href="https://jeffandersonlogic.github.io/BeCurrent/iran/study-guide.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Iran at War study guide</a>.</li>
</ul>

<h3>Step 4: Save it with your notes in it</h3>
<ol>
    <li>Click the <strong>Download</strong> button (the arrow pointing down) in the top right corner of Chrome. You can also press <strong>Ctrl + S</strong>.</li>
    <li>If Chrome asks, choose <strong>With your changes</strong>.</li>
    <li>Name the file with your name, like <strong>Lastname Firstname Reference Guide</strong>, and click <strong>Save</strong>.</li>
</ol>
<p><strong>Do not just close the tab.</strong> If you close it without saving, your notes are gone.</p>

<h3>Step 5: Check your saved copy</h3>
<p>Open the file you just saved (Files, then Downloads). Make sure your notes are in the boxes. If the boxes are empty, go back to Step 4 and save again.</p>

<h3>Step 6: Upload it here</h3>
<ol>
    <li>At the top of this page, click <strong>Start Assignment</strong>.</li>
    <li>Click <strong>Upload File</strong> and choose the guide you saved in Step 4.</li>
    <li>Click <strong>Submit Assignment</strong>.</li>
</ol>

<h3>Step 7: Check what you turned in</h3>
<p>After you submit, click your file&rsquo;s name on the right side of this page. Make sure your notes show up. This is the guide you will use on the test, so check it now.</p>

<h3>Need to fix something?</h3>
<p>You can turn in a new version until the test opens. Open your saved file in Chrome, make your changes, save it again (Step 4), and upload it again (Step 6). The last file you turn in is the one you use.</p>

<h3>On test day</h3>
<p>Open this assignment and click your file&rsquo;s name to open your guide. Use only this guide.</p>

<h3>If something goes wrong</h3>
<ul>
    <li><strong>I cannot type in the boxes.</strong> You are not in Chrome. Go back to Step 2.</li>
    <li><strong>A box stopped taking text.</strong> The box is full. Shorten what you wrote.</li>
    <li><strong>My notes disappeared.</strong> The file was saved without your changes. Fill it in again and follow Step 4 carefully.</li>
    <li><strong>Canvas will not take my file.</strong> It must be the PDF from Step 4. Other file types are not accepted.</li>
    <li><strong>Still stuck?</strong> Ask me before the test, not during it.</li>
</ul>
```

## Lock the test until the guide is submitted

The test and the guide share their own module, after the unit module:

```
Module: Current Events - Iran at War - Unit Test
[Assignment]  IR - Test Reference Guide     requirement: submit the assignment
[Quiz]        IR - Unit Test               requirement: submit
```

1. Create the module and add the two items in that order.
2. In the module's **Edit** menu, add requirements and choose
   **Students must complete all of these requirements**.
3. Set `IR - Test Reference Guide` to **submit the assignment**.
4. Tick **Students must move through requirements in sequential order**.
   This is the lock: the test stays locked for a student until their guide
   is submitted, wherever they try to open it from.
5. Rename `IR - Unit Test` to the real name of the test, if it differs.
6. Check it in **Student View** before publishing: the test must show as
   locked, then open once the Test Student submits a guide.

**Submitting unlocks the test, not a good guide.** An empty upload unlocks it
too. To require a reviewed guide instead, set the requirement to
**score at least** a value and grade the guides before the test opens; the
cost is that a guide you have not graded yet keeps a student locked out.

## What the limits can and cannot do

Every box has one locked font and size, takes plain text only, and stops
typing at its edge. Each character limit is measured at build time as what
that box can show, so a student can fill a box but a paste cannot hide text
below it. The file is permission-locked: it opens with no password and its
boxes can be filled, but the form, its fields and its fonts cannot be edited.

Chrome's PDF viewer, which is what a Chromebook uses, and Adobe Acrobat and
Reader enforce all of that, and a paste is cut off at the limit rather than
squeezed in. Check one Test Student submission opens in SpeedGrader before
the class submits, since the file is locked. A tool that writes on top
of a PDF instead of filling its boxes, such as Kami or the Canvas annotation
tools, does not. A guide with typing outside the boxes, or a different file
entirely, is not this guide: open a few submissions before the test.
